claims.text: The initial material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform microstructure.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce accelerated coupled degradation.
Thermally activated diffusion is a primary driver of the accelerated coupled degradation.
Mechanical stress-induced grain-boundary migration is a primary driver of the accelerated coupled degradation.
Thermally activated diffusion and grain-boundary migration act synergistically.
The proposed processes enhance transport of corrosive species along grain boundaries.
The proposed processes enhance transport of wear-generated debris along grain boundaries.
Grain boundaries and phase interfaces are the relevant structural mediators.
The wear exposure uses a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and a normal load of 50 N.
The corrosion exposure consists of 1 atm humid air and 0.1% NaCl solution.
Coupled exposure will increase total degradation by 30% relative to the stated baseline.
Coupled exposure will increase wear rate by 25% relative to the stated baseline.
Coupled exposure will increase corrosion rate by 40% relative to the stated baseline.
Grain-boundary engineering should produce a significant change in degradation behavior if the proposed grain-boundary mechanism is operative.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies 800 °C at 1 atm, while the corrosion condition is described as a NaCl solution without explaining how a liquid solution is maintained under those conditions.

A single 'matched baseline' is described as exposure to individual wear or corrosion, which actually defines two different controls and leaves the reference for total degradation and each component response ambiguous.
The falsification rule combines p > 0.05 with a 10% effect-size threshold, but it does not specify how to decide when statistical significance and the 10% threshold disagree.
